reasoning_traces.think:
The paper attempts to quantify whether weather data improves photovoltaic power prediction but fails due to flawed methodology. It uses random splits on time-ordered data, introducing temporal leakage. The lack of clear units and scaling undermines interpretability. Without an ablation study comparing models with and without weather inputs, it cannot answer its own title question. The claim that ~6 features suffice is based on unstable validation practices. These issues render the primitives non-transferable to GSI or GSE because they lack robustness, causality, and reproducibility. The core operators—feature utility assessment, validation design, and ablation—are mathematically unsound for forecasting tasks where temporal integrity is essential.
